answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The river multiplier is published, charged in hollow, and comet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3887 identities would post 1331 proofs and burn roughly 3 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
